{{Quote|Our scout ships have reached Dantooine. They found the remains of a Rebel base, but they estimate that it has been deserted for some time. They are now conducting an extensive search of the surrounding systems.|Siward Cass reports to Grand Moff Wilhuff Tarkin|audio=Cass-ANH.flac|<ref name="ANH" />}}
'''Siward Cass''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[bureaucrat]] and military [[officer]] who served as a [[major]] and later [[chief]] under the [[Galactic Empire]], the [[Proclamation of the New Order|successor]] state of the [[Galactic Republic]]. By the early stages of the [[Galactic Civil War]], Cass was stationed on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|DS-1 Death Star Mobile Battle Station]], the Empire's planet-killing [[superweapon]], serving as an [[aide]] to the station's commander, [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]].

Around this [[time]], Cass attended a meeting of the [[Joint Chiefs of the Imperial Military|Joint Chiefs]], in which various high-ranking military officers debated the purported threat that the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] posed. Shortly thereafter, the captive [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] of [[Alderaan]] lied and told Tarkin that the rebel's [[Massassi Site|hidden base]] was on [[Dantooine]]. When it was discovered that, while there had been a [[Dantooine base|base]] on Dantooine, it had been deserted for some time, Cass delivered the news to Tarkin. 

==Biography==
===Early career===
Within [[4 BBY]],<ref name="SWR:SOTE4-Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''Servants of the Empire: The Secret Academy'' to [[4 BBY]].</ref> during the [[Imperial Era]], the [[human]]<ref name="ANH" /> [[Gender|male]] Siward<ref name="Incident" /> Cass held the [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[Military rank|rank]] of [[major]], and the [[officer]] served as an [[aide]] to [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]], [[governor]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories]]. At this [[time]], there were rumors that [[Commandant]] [[Brendol Hux]] had created a [[Commandant's Cadets|secret society]] within the [[Arkanis Academy]]. On Tarkin's order, Cass transferred [[Lieutenant]] [[Chiron]] from the [[Academy for Young Imperials]] on [[Lothal]] to [[Arkanis]] so he could investigate the matter. The major notably made sure that Chiron's [[code cylinder]] would give him access to [[Area Null]], a restricted part of the [[Imperial Academy|academy]] where the Empire ran a number of secret programs.<ref name="TSA">''[[Servants of the Empire: The Secret Academy]]''</ref>

===The Death Star===
Siward Cass was still serving under Tarkin during the [[Galactic Civil War]], which pitted the Empire against [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="ANH" /> At this time, he was a [[Chief]].<ref name="Incident" /> Shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin]], the [[Imperial Army]] [[Imperial officer|officer]] attended a meeting on board the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] in which he witnessed [[Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti]] and [[General]] [[Cassio Tagge]] argue about the [[Space station|station's]] power, before the [[Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] [[Force choke]]d Motti. He later reported to Tarkin that the [[planet]] [[Dantooine]] was not the location of the main Rebel base. Not too long afterward, the Battle of [[Yavin Prime|Yavin]] commenced, with the Alliance destroying the [[Death Star]] [[battle station]].<ref name="ANH" />

==Equipment and uniform==
[[File:Cabadge.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Cass's rank insignia]]
Siward Cass used the [[Imperial Military]]'s standard-issue olive colored uniform consisting of an [[Imperial military uniforms|officer's tunic]], a pair of flared pants, a black [[utility belt]], and a pair of black [[durasteel]]-toed [[boot]]s. He also wore a single row [[rank insignia plaque]] of four [[Color|yellow]] tiles followed by two red tiles.<ref name="ANH" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Portrayal in ''Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope''===
Siward Cass first appeared portrayed by English actor [[Patrick Jordan]] in the [[1977]] original ''[[Star Wars]]'' film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], the first installment of the [[original trilogy]]. Though unnamed in the movie itself,<ref name="ANH" /> he was referred as "Cass" in [[Alan Dean Foster]]'s [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]].<ref name="ANHn">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'' novel]]</ref> Jordan got the part of Cass in ''A New Hope'' through his friendship with [[Alec Guinness]], who portrayed [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and whom had worked with Jordan for [[Wikipedia:The Old Vic|The Old Vic]] company in the [[1940s]]. However, Jordan shared Guinness' contempt for the film, dubious about the film's prospects.<ref>{{WebCite|Date=2020-02-10|url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2020/feb/10/patrick-jordan-obituary|text=Patrick Jordan obituary|author=Weaver, Matthew|archivedate=20200213104356}}</ref>

===Fan developments===
Although Cass was sometimes identified as a [[General/Legends|general]] by fan-created sources,<ref name="theforce">{{WebCite|url=http://theforce.net/swtc/insignia/badges.html#mjgeneral|text=theforce.net|archivedate=20011109130830}}</ref> he was initially only referred to in [[canon]] as "Imperial Officer Cass" or "Officer Cass," and his exact rank long remained unknown. Unlike most characters whose names are known in the script, Officer Cass does not have an entry in the [[StarWars.com]] official [[Databank (original)|Databank]].

In [[2013]], Cass was eventually given the first name "Siward" and the position of "Chief" in both the ''[[Death Star Owner's Technical Manual]]''<ref name="DSOTM">''[[Death Star Owner's Technical Manual]]''</ref> and the article [[A Certain Point of View (department)|''The Death Star Coup'']], written by [[Jason Fry]] for the [[Star Wars Insider Special Edition 2014|Special Edition 2014]] of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine.<ref name="SWI">{{InsiderCite|Special Edition 2014|A Certain Point of View|A Certain Point of View: The Death Star Coup}}</ref> Jason Fry selected the character's first name as a homage to another character featured in [[Wikipedia:William Shakespeare|William Shakespeare's]] play [[Wikipedia:Macbeth|''Macbeth'']], named [[Wikipedia:Siward, Earl of Northumbria|Siward, Earl of Northumberland]], who was general of the English forces within that narrative.<ref name="Twit2">{{Twitter|jasoncfry|status/396712749956218880|[[Jason Fry]]|nobackup=1}}</ref> According to [[Chris Trevas]], one of the co-authors of the ''Technical Manual'', Cass was given that position because his rank insignia plaque was the same one as [[Moradmin Bast/Legends|Moradmin Bast's]],<ref name="Siward Cass's position">{{Facebook|username=StarWarsSourcebooks|url=StarWarsSourcebooks/posts/634665586583552|name=Chris Trevas|date=30-10-2013|quote=Cass is now labeled Chief since his rank badge matches Bast's. Jason's Insider article may have more info.|archivedate=20200820185325}}</ref> who was first identified as "Chief Bast" in the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] [[Premiere Limited]] expansion set.<ref name="ccg">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Chief Bast}}</ref> Later, in [[2015]] a card within the canonical [[Star Wars: Card Trader|''Star Wars'': Card Trader]] game from [[Topps]] implied that Bast's position of "Chief" was a shortened title of his full position as "chief manager", and he was also established to be a [[general]] within the [[Imperial Army]].<ref name="SWCT">{{SWCT|set=Base Series 1|cardname=Chief Bast - Imperial Aide}}</ref> Despite Cass possessing identical rank insignia to Bast<ref name="ANH" /> and a short story in the anthology collection ''[[From a Certain Point of View|From a Certain Point of View: A New Hope]]'' also stating he held the position of "Chief" akin to Bast,<ref name="Incident" /> currently no canonical source has clarified if Cass also served as a general (like his namesake) and was a chief manager.
